[[File:Manny Malhotra - Montreal Canadiens.jpg|thumb|[[Manny Malhotra]] is the current head coach of the Canucks.]]
The [[Vancouver Canucks]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Vancouver]]. They are a member of the [[Pacific Division (NHL)|Pacific Division]] in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/nhl/app?service=page&page=StandingsPage&type=DIV|title=Standings|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|access-date=2008-07-22}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} </ref> The team plays its home games at [[Rogers Arena]]. The Canucks joined the NHL in 1970 as an [[expansion team]], along with the [[Buffalo Sabres]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.andrewsstarspage.com/NHL-Business/Expansion.htm|title=NHL Expansion & Relocation Since 1967|publisher=AndrewsStarsPage.com|access-date=2008-07-22|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080620072720/http://andrewsstarspage.com/NHL-Business/Expansion.htm|archive-date=2008-06-20}}</ref> They have advanced to the [[Stanley Cup Final]] three times but were defeated by the [[New York Islanders]] in [[1982 Stanley Cup Final|1982]], the [[New York Rangers]] in [[1994 Stanley Cup Final|1994]], and the [[Boston Bruins]] in [[2011 Stanley Cup Final|2011]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629213230/http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2009-06-29 |title=Stanley Cup Champions and Finalists |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |access-date=2008-07-24 }}</ref> The Canucks are owned by [[Francesco Aquilini]], and [[Ryan Johnson (ice hockey, born 1976)|Ryan Johnson]] is their [[general manager]], and [[Manny Malhotra]] is their [[Coach (ice hockey)|head coach]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://canucks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=12865 |title=Front Office |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |access-date=2009-05-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090417051705/http://canucks.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=12865 |archive-date=2009-04-17 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://canucks.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |title=Roster |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |access-date=2009-05-17 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090627023007/http://canucks.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |archive-date=2009-06-27 }}</ref>

There have been 23 [[head coach]]es for the Canucks. The franchise's first head coach was [[Hal Laycoe]], who coached the Canucks for two seasons. [[Alain Vigneault]] coached the most games of any Canucks head coach with 540 games and has the most points all-time with the Canucks with 683 points, he also has the most points in a season of any Canucks coach, with 117 in the [[2010–11 NHL season|2010–11 season]]. He is followed by [[Marc Crawford]], who has 586 points all-time with the Canucks, while [[Roger Neilson]] is the only [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] inductee to coach the Canucks. [[Pat Quinn (ice hockey)|Pat Quinn]], Vigneault and [[Rick Tocchet]] are the only Canucks head coaches to win a [[Jack Adams Award]] with the team. [[Bill LaForge]], who coached at the beginning of the [[1984–85 NHL season|1984–85 season]], has the fewest points with the Canucks (10). [[Harry Neale]] served the most terms as head coach of the Canucks with three, while Pat Quinn served twice.
